definition_en: attractive in a pretty or endearing way
core_image: 一只圆眼的小狗坐在篮子边，歪着头看人
scene: 一只圆眼的小狗坐在篮子边，歪着头看人。 The puppy looks very cute.
sceneCN: 这里 cute 是「可爱的」（第 01 个义项）；句意是这只小狗看起来可爱极了。

senses.title: Pretty and endearing
senses.definition: attractive in a pretty or endearing way, especially a small animal or child
senses.definitionCN: 小巧、好看又让人心生喜爱的样子，多形容小动物或孩子
senses.example: The puppy looks very cute.
senses.exampleCN: 这只小狗看起来可爱极了。
senses.why: Cute is a shortened form of acute, which meant sharp; from "sharp-looking" it slid into "small and pleasing to look at".
senses.whyCN: cute 是 acute（尖锐的）的缩略形式，从「看起来机灵」滑向「小巧好看、讨人喜欢」。

senses.title: Clever in an annoying way
senses.definition: trying to be clever or tricky, in a way that annoys people
senses.definitionCN: 故意卖弄机灵、耍花招，让人不快
senses.example: Don't get cute with the teacher.
senses.why: The "sharp" meaning inside cute survived: a person being cute is being too sharp, trying to outwit others instead of behaving plainly.
senses.whyCN: cute 里「尖锐」那层意思还在：说一个人 cute，就是说他太精，想靠小聪明压过别人。

definition_en: a journey to a place and back, to catch your foot and fall, or a mistake
core_image: 一家人提着行李出门，准备坐车去海边玩两天

senses.title: A journey to a place and back
senses.definition: A journey to a place and back
senses.example: We took a trip to the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 我们去海边旅行了一趟。

senses.whyCN: 轻快的脚步会被东西挂住，动词便指这种踉跄。

definition_en: to move through water using the body, to move smoothly, or to feel dizzy
core_image: 下午的泳池里，孩子们套着浮圈，手脚一起划水
scene: 下午的泳池里，孩子们套着浮圈，手脚一起划水 In the afternoon pool the children wear floats and swim with arms and legs together.
sceneCN: 这里 swim 是「游泳」（第 01 个义项）；句意是夏天我们在河里游泳。

senses.title: To move through water using the body
senses.definition: To move through water using the body
senses.example: We swim in the river in summer.
senses.why: Old English swimman meant to move through water, a very old Germanic verb.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 swimman 意为在水中移动，是极古老的日耳曼语动词。

senses.title: To move smoothly as if in water

senses.definitionCN: 像在水里一样平滑移动
senses.example: The fish swam around the rock.
senses.why: Water motion gave the word to anything that moves in that gliding way.
senses.whyCN: 水中的动作为这种滑行方式提供了词义。

senses.title: To feel dizzy
senses.definition: To feel dizzy
senses.example: The room swam before my eyes.
senses.why: When the world seems to move like water, English says the head or room swims.
senses.whyCN: 当世界像水一样晃动时，英语说头或房间在游动。

definition_en: to make something go from one place to another, or to order someone to go somewhere
core_image: 信封贴上邮票被投进邮筒，远处校门口老师正送学生出校
scene: 信封贴上邮票被投进邮筒，远处校门口老师正送学生出校。 I will send the letter tomorrow.
sceneCN: 这里 send 是「寄送」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我明天寄这封信。

senses.title: To make a letter or parcel go somewhere
senses.definition: To make a letter or parcel go somewhere
senses.definitionCN: 把信件或包裹送到别处
senses.example: I will send the letter tomorrow.
senses.why: Old English sendan meant to cause to go; the word has kept that sense of making something travel.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 sendan 意为使…去，这个词一直保留着让某物上路的含义。

senses.title: To order someone to go somewhere
senses.definition: To order someone to go somewhere
senses.example: The school sent him to the contest.
senses.why: The same idea applies to people: to send a person is to make that person go on an errand or a mission.
senses.whyCN: 同一思路也用于人：send 一个人，就是让他去办事或执行任务。

senses.title: To transmit a signal or message
senses.definition: To transmit a signal or message
senses.example: Send me a message when you arrive.
senses.why: With radio and phones the word moved from paper to signals, still meaning making something travel to another place.
senses.whyCN: 到了广播与电话时代，这个词从纸面转到信号，仍指把东西传到另一处。

definition_en: a very large animal that lived long ago and is now extinct
core_image: 博物馆里一具高大的恐龙骨架，孩子在它脚下仰头看
scene: 博物馆里一具高大的恐龙骨架，孩子在它脚下仰头看。 A dinosaur skeleton stands in the museum hall.
sceneCN: 这里 dinosaur 是「恐龙」（第 01 个义项）；句意是博物馆大厅里立着一具恐龙骨架。

senses.title: A large extinct animal of the distant past
senses.definition: a large animal with four legs and a long tail that lived millions of years ago and is now extinct
senses.definitionCN: 数百万年前生活、如今已灭绝的大型四足长尾动物
senses.example: A dinosaur skeleton stands in the museum hall.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆大厅里立着一具恐龙骨架。
senses.why: Greek deinos, terrible, plus sauros, lizard, gave dinosaur, the "terrible lizard" named by a Victorian scientist for the giant fossil bones.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 deinos（可怕的）加 sauros（蜥蜴）构成 dinosaur，维多利亚时代的学者见到巨大化石，把它命名为「可怕的蜥蜴」。

senses.title: Someone or something hopelessly out of date
senses.definition: a person or thing that is old-fashioned and cannot adapt
senses.definitionCN: 跟不上时代、无法适应的人或事物
senses.example: The old typewriter is a dinosaur in a modern office.
senses.exampleCN: 在现代办公室里，那台旧打字机是个老古董。
senses.why: Dinosaurs died out while the world changed, so the name became a metaphor for anything that cannot keep up and disappears.
senses.whyCN: 恐龙在世界改变时灭绝了，这个名字就被用来比喻跟不上变化、终将消失的事物。

definition_en: a piece of ground for flowers, for vegetables, or around a house
core_image: 屋后的小花园里，玫瑰沿着木栅栏开花
scene: 屋后的小花园里，玫瑰沿着木栅栏开花。 There are roses in the garden.
sceneCN: 这里 garden 是「花园」（第 01 个义项）；句意是花园里有玫瑰。

senses.title: A piece of ground where flowers grow
senses.definition: ground where flowers are grown
senses.example: There are roses in the garden.
senses.why: Garden comes from Old Northern French gardin, from a Germanic word for an enclosure; a garden is ground enclosed and tended.
senses.whyCN: garden 源自古北部法语 gardin，出自日耳曼语表示「围起来的地方」的词；花园就是围起来并加以照料的地。

senses.title: A plot where vegetables are grown
senses.definition: a plot where vegetables are grown
senses.example: We grow tomatoes in the vegetable garden.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在菜园里种西红柿。
senses.why: The same enclosed ground, when planted with food rather than flowers, is called a garden of vegetables.
senses.whyCN: 同一块围起来的地，若种的是吃的而不是花，就叫菜园。

senses.title: The ground around a house
senses.definition: the ground around a house
senses.example: The children play in the back garden.
senses.why: In British use the tended ground around a house is the garden, whether or not it has flowers.
senses.whyCN: 在英式用法里，房子周围经过照料的地都叫 garden，不管有没有花。

definition_en: the father of one of your parents, or a male ancestor

senses.definition: a male ancestor
senses.example: His grandfathers came from the north.
senses.why: Because a grandfather stands one generation back, the plural grandfathers can name the male ancestors further back still.

definition_en: to go past, to pass a test, to hand over, or a card that lets you in
